To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the hippocampus of young rats is vulnerable to SE and this is associated with increased expression of TrkB, which is a marker of neuroplasticity and neurogenesis.

the hippocampal levels of BDNF mRNA and TrkB protein are increased in the early stages of the epileptogenic process, and this increase is associated with increased seizure activity and neuronal hyperexcitability.

(1) the hippocampal BDNT mRNA and protein expression were significantly increased 1 and 3 days after the SE, and the TrkB mRNA expression was significantly increased 3 days after SE; and (2) the BDNF protein levels were significantly increased in the hippocampus 3 days after status epilepticis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of BDNF and its receptor TrkB in the pathogenesis of status epilepticus and the development of epilepsy in young animals.
the effects of the status epilepticus on the brain and the possible mechanisms of the neuroprotection.
the effects of status epilepticus in the developing rat hippocampus and the role of BDNF and trkB in the regulation of neuronal plasticity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BDNF and trkB are involved in the pathogenesis of epilepsy and that they play an important role in neuronal survival, synaptic plasticity and neuronal repair.
BDNF and its receptor TrkB are involved in the regulation of the hippocampal excitability and plasticity.

the results of the present study show that there are no significant differences in the expression of BDNF and/or its receptor, TrkB, between rats that had been subjected to status epilepticus at 7 days of age and control animals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BDNF and its receptor TrkB are upregulated after status epilepticis.
the hippocampus, a brain region important for learning and memory, is vulnerable to the neurotoxic effects of seizures.

the expression of the BDNF gene in the hippocampus is increased by status epilepticus, which is accompanied by a significant increase in the level of BDNF in the hippocampus, and that these changes persist for at least 2 months.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have developed a new method to study the effects of status epilepticus (SE) on the developing brain.
there is a strong relationship between the hippocampal expression of BDNF and the severity of status epilepticus-induced brain injury.
the brain can be reprogrammed to produce new neurons and this can be used to treat neurological disorders.
